target_customer: Adult consumers who drink alcohol, buying direct online and later at retail
problem: Hangovers come from acetaldehyde, a toxic alcohol byproduct, and existing remedies did not address it directly.
business_model: Direct to consumer sales of a pre-alcohol probiotic drink, later Amazon and retail

founders.name: Zack Abbott
education: PhD in microbiology and immunology, University of Michigan

founders.name: Stephen Lamb
education: JD and MBA, University of Pennsylvania Law School and Wharton
founders.background_notes: YC page lists corporate real estate management, new market entry and cross-border transactions experience.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering Bacillus subtilis to express an acetaldehyde enzyme needed synthetic biology, safety testing and US regulatory navigation. In July 2018 only in vitro tests existed and no human trials.

defensibility.rationale: A patented engineered strain (ZB183) and safety work are hard to copy, while generic hangover supplements are easy to launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found; the company stayed independent and reached profitability in 2023.

market_need_then: Hangover remedies were a broad consumer category and traditional probiotics a 40 billion dollar industry per TechCrunch in 2018. Demand was untested at the time since no clinical data existed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Open about genetic engineering; trade press uses the phrase proudly GMO

branding.brand_signature: Proudly GMO positioning and the Pre-Alcohol product name
branding.community_and_virality: Press attention including TechCrunch, Genetic Literacy Project and wedding trend coverage; 15 million plus shots reported sold.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear product name (Pre-Alcohol) and a bold GMO stance drew trade press, but no source shows the brand name itself as a growth driver.

outcome_analysis: ZBiotics engineered a probiotic that breaks down acetaldehyde, raised a 2.8 million seed in 2018, launched direct to consumer in 2019 and more than doubled sales each year, reaching company-wide profitability in 2023. It closed a 12 million Series A in August 2024 to expand into retail. It is active with about 22 staff.
notes: Competitors: the July 2018 TechCrunch article names none, so the list is empty. Aggregators list conflicting rounds (22.4M Series A in 2024, 5.69M Series A in 2020 led by Oyster Ventures, totals 14.3M to 40.3M); unverified and not recorded. A crowdfunding campaign was planned for late 2018; its result not verified. Business Wire press release returned 403.
